===============================================================
  MAP LICENSE - GUIDE FOR MAP AUTHORS
  Minecraft 1.21.11 / Fabric        Mod by Hi_Its_I
===============================================================

This mod locks one specific world behind a one-time activation
code. A buyer enters their code once, and it is bound to their
Minecraft account from then on.

There is no license server. Everything needed to check a code
ships inside the jar, so you do not have to host or pay for
anything.


---------------------------------------------------------------
  READ THIS FIRST - WHAT IT DOES AND DOES NOT DO
---------------------------------------------------------------

It stops:

  * "download the leaked zip and play"  - the files alone are
    not enough, a code is needed
  * unpacking the jar to find codes     - only hashes ship in
    it, and there is no key inside to mint new ones
  * one buyer sharing their code around - spent after the first
    use on that computer, and with account-bound codes useless
    to anyone else at all

It does not stop:

  * a leaked POOL code being used again on a different
    computer. Without a server there is nowhere to record that
    a code was already spent, so it works again on a fresh
    install. Use account-bound codes (below) where this
    matters.
  * taking a code back once it is out. There is no server to
    push a revocation to.
  * a cracked launcher that lets its user set any UUID. Bound
    codes stop code sharing between real accounts, not that.
  * somebody editing the jar. Any check running on the player's
    own machine can be removed by someone determined enough.

Account-bound codes are the answer to a leaked code being used
by strangers. What still needs a real license server is taking
back a code you already handed out, and proving an account is
genuine. This mod is the version that costs nothing to run.


---------------------------------------------------------------
  WHAT YOU WERE GIVEN, AND WHAT YOU NEED
---------------------------------------------------------------

In the folder:

  src/ build.gradle gradlew ...   the mod source
  tools/generate_codes.py         the code generator
  dist/READ-ME-FIRST.txt          template to send to buyers
  dist/issue-codes.yml            optional GitHub Actions
                                  workflow for minting codes
  dist/map_license_colab.ipynb    do all of this in a browser
                                  instead, with nothing installed
  README.md, USAGE.md             fuller documentation

You need JDK 21 and Python 3. Gradle is not a separate install -
the wrapper in the folder fetches it.

If you would rather install nothing at all, open
dist/map_license_colab.ipynb in Google Colab
(colab.research.google.com -> Upload). It walks through steps 1
to 5 below as fill-in-the-blank forms and hands you the finished
jar. You still need to read STEP 2 - no notebook can wire your
map's progression for you.

You build this yourself rather than being handed a finished jar,
because the world it protects and the codes it accepts are both
compiled into the jar. A prebuilt one would be locked to
somebody else's map and somebody else's codes.

Do these three before your first release:

  1. Put your own world's details in gate.json      (STEP 1)
  2. Mint your own codes                            (STEP 3)
  3. Change the INTEGRITY_KEY string in
     src/main/java/net/jihoon/maplicense/LicenseStore.java
     to any other text, so activation records from another
     build do not validate against yours


---------------------------------------------------------------
  STEP 1 - POINT THE MOD AT YOUR WORLD
---------------------------------------------------------------

Open your finished map with the mod installed, and run this as
an operator:

        /maplicense fingerprint

It prints the world's name and seed. Put them into
src/main/resources/map-license/gate.json :

        {
            "mapId": "my-story-map",
            "title": "My Story Map",
            "markerFile": "map-license.json",
            "worldNames": ["my story map"],
            "seeds": [-4172144997902289642],
            "lockTimeoutSeconds": 300
        }

Any one of the three signals - world name, seed, or a marker
file in the world folder - is enough to trigger the lock. They
overlap on purpose: a marker file can be deleted and a folder
can be renamed, but the seed lives in level.dat and changing it
desyncs any terrain that was not pre-generated.

This file is compiled into the jar, not read from the config
folder. A file the player can edit is a file the player can
empty.


---------------------------------------------------------------
  STEP 2 - MAKE THE MOD LOAD-BEARING  (IMPORTANT)
---------------------------------------------------------------

If someone simply deletes the mod, nothing runs and nothing is
locked. The mod cannot prevent that by itself. What it gives
you instead is a hook your map can depend on.

Every player's licence state is mirrored into a scoreboard
objective named "maplicense":

        execute if score @s maplicense matches 1 run \
            function mymap:chapter1/start

Wire your map's progression - doors, chapter triggers, story
functions - through that score. A world opened without the mod
never has the objective at all, so the score is never 1 and the
story never advances.

Skip this step and the mod is only a speed bump. Do it, and
removing the mod breaks the map instead of freeing it.


---------------------------------------------------------------
  STEP 3 - MINT YOUR CODES
---------------------------------------------------------------

There are two kinds, and they behave very differently once a
code leaks. You can use both.

POOL CODES - any account can redeem them

        python3 tools/generate_codes.py --count 200 \
            --out-codes tools/codes-batch1.txt \
            --out-hashes src/main/resources/map-license/codes.json

Mint these in bulk ahead of time and hand out one line per sale.
If a buyer publishes their code, everyone who has it can use it,
because nothing outside their own computer knows it was spent.

ACCOUNT-BOUND CODES - one account, and only that one

        python3 tools/generate_codes.py --count 1 \
            --for-player Notch \
            --out-codes tools/codes-notch.txt \
            --out-hashes src/main/resources/map-license/codes.json

The buyer's account UUID is mixed into the stored hash, so the
same code typed on any other account produces a different hash
and is rejected. A leaked bound code is useless to whoever
receives it.

The cost is that you cannot mint these in advance - you need the
buyer's Minecraft username first, so every sale means minting
and rebuilding. If you keep the mod in a GitHub repository, copy
dist/issue-codes.yml into .github/workflows/ and that becomes
one button on the Actions tab: fill in the buyer's username, and
the run mints the code, rebuilds, and hands you both.

Use --for-uuid <uuid> instead of --for-player if you are offline
or already know the UUID.

The plaintext file records which account a bound batch belongs
to on its first line. Keep that line - the codes themselves look
identical either way:

        # bound to account 069a79f4-44e9-4726-a5be-fca90e38aaf5
        J8G9-AW14-25H9-742P

WARNING: a bound code entered on the wrong account reports
"That code is not valid", exactly like a made-up code. The jar
holds only hashes, so it cannot tell the two apart. When a buyer
says their code does not work, check the username you bound it
to before anything else.

Either way, the run writes two files:

  tools/codes-batch1.txt
        The real codes. These are what you sell. THIS IS THE
        ONLY COPY THAT WILL EVER EXIST - they cannot be
        recovered from the jar. Back it up, and never ship it.

  codes.json
        Hashes only. This is what goes into the jar.

Running it again against the same codes.json keeps the salt and
ADDS to the list, so a second batch does not kill the first.

Mint generously the first time. 5,000 codes add about 166 KB to
the jar, which is nothing next to a map, and it saves you
rebuilding every time you need more.


---------------------------------------------------------------
  STEP 4 - BUILD
---------------------------------------------------------------

        ./gradlew clean build

The jar lands in build/libs/ . Ship the one with the HIGHEST
version number - it recognises the codes from every batch you
have minted so far.

Codes only work in a jar built AFTER they were minted. If you
mint a batch and forget to rebuild, every code in it will be
rejected.


---------------------------------------------------------------
  STEP 5 - PACKAGE AND SELL
---------------------------------------------------------------

Send each buyer a zip like this:

        MyStoryMap.zip
        +-- READ-ME-FIRST.txt      (fill in the placeholders)
        +-- map-license-1.2.0.jar  (highest version)
        +-- MyStoryMap/            (the world folder)

READ-ME-FIRST.txt has four placeholders. The code differs per
buyer, so this file is filled in once per sale:

        [MAP NAME]         your map's name
        [YOUR CODE HERE]   one line from your batch file
        [SUPPORT CONTACT]  your email or Discord
        [YOUR NAME HERE]   your name

Check none survived before sending:

        grep -n "\[[A-Z ]*\]" READ-ME-FIRST.txt

Keep a record of which code went to which order. Nothing tracks
that for you, and you will need it the first time somebody asks
for help.


---------------------------------------------------------------
  RUNNING IT DAY TO DAY
---------------------------------------------------------------

Operator commands:

        /maplicense fingerprint       show this world's name/seed
        /maplicense revoke <player>   unbind an account

"revoke" is for the case where a code got bound to the wrong
account. The code itself stays spent afterwards, so unbinding
does not create a code that works twice - give the player a
fresh code from your batch.

Buyer says their code is rejected:
        If it is a bound code, check the username you bound it
        to - a typo there looks exactly like an invalid code.
        Otherwise their jar is probably older than their code,
        so send them the current one.

Buyer got a new computer:
        They enter the same code again. Activation is stored in
        config/map-license/activations.json on their machine,
        so a fresh install has no record of it.


---------------------------------------------------------------
  RULES THAT WILL BITE YOU IF YOU BREAK THEM
---------------------------------------------------------------

  1. Never ship, commit, or publish tools/codes*.txt .
     That file is every unsold code you own.

  2. Never hand-edit codes.json, and never change its salt.
     Every code you already sold stops working.

  3. Change the INTEGRITY_KEY string in LicenseStore.java
     before your first release, so activation records from
     someone else's build do not validate against yours.

  4. Always rebuild after minting, and always ship the highest
     version number.


---------------------------------------------------------------
  CREDITS
---------------------------------------------------------------

  Licensing mod    Hi_Its_I

  Free to use for your own maps. The limits described at the
  top are real - please be honest with your buyers about them
  rather than promising protection this cannot deliver.
